verdict_reason: 9 of 458 red-capable sites were re-read from their own source: 1 measures a copy lag (an upstream mtime, so an arbitrarily old face stays green while the panel is behind its input), 2 pin a face field to a frozen date literal and therefore red on an honest refresh, 6 carry no date comparison at all and the line E411 called a date comparison compares a column count. After reclassification 0 of 408 faces have a reader that can go red on age (published: 9 protected), 116 blind faces have no writer on the round chain, and 2 of the faces the suite reads declare any freshness expectation at all -- both of the declared ones sit on faces this tier table never priced. The chain does not save them either: of 17 priced faces it RUNS a writer for 7 and only VERIFIES 8, so each frozen gate sits on a face whose refresh the chain deliberately refuses.

method_limits: the tier vocabulary, the site list and the per-face writer class are E411's published rows; this study re-reads the four sites' own source blocks and re-prices the faces, it does not re-run E408's 46 s writer census
a site is called an age test only when a clock/calendar token appears on a line that also carries a comparison; a clock token read for printing is not an age gate
the frozen-constant arm keys on a literal YYYY-MM-DD compared to a .get() field of the same block, so a gate that pins a date through a module constant is not counted
writer_runs_per_round is E411's class, which answers 'does a registered task or chain leg run the writer', not 'has it run since this face was written'
this study reads faces and never writes them: refreshing an input destroys the evidence that the input was stale
